cap: Negative feedback makes the trophic and target hormones move in opposite directions when the gland itself is the problem, and in the same direction when the pituitary or hypothalamus is the problem. A high hormone with signs of deficiency means the target cells cannot respond: androgen insensitivity (high LH and testosterone), pseudohypoparathyroidism (high PTH, low calcium) and Laron syndrome (high GH, low IGF-1).
teach: Read a panel in two steps. First decide whether the tissues show too much or too little hormone effect. Then compare the direction of the trophic hormone with the target hormone. Opposite directions put the lesion in the gland; the same direction puts it upstream, or in a tumor that makes the trophic hormone, and the clinical picture separates excess from resistance.
